title: feat(scripts): report-only skill-example schema probe — ruling B step one readings
body:
Part of #22059
Clause-②: no

Step ① of ruling B (comment 6050857613): **the probe and its readings, not the gate.** It adds a report-only mode, `node scripts/check-corpus-claim-drift.mjs --probe-examples [--json FILE]`, backed by a new module `scripts/skill-example-probe.mjs`. The mode exits 0 on any reading. It is wired into no `check:*` script, no workflow and no baseline. The drift script's `--self-test` gains four `Probe …` batteries (65 cases) that pin the probe's pure parts over synthetic schemas, so neither the self-test nor the ratchet needs a build.

## Headline

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| **hit rate, cards filed before #22059 with a landed published-catalog repair** | **2 / 19 (10.5%)** |
| hit rate, every card the premise listing matched at filing | 2 / 20 (10.0%) |
| hit rate, every card the listing matches today | 2 / 22 (9.1%) |
| the ruling's bar | one half |
| ceiling with a perfect transform (cards whose repair changed example *code*) | 6 / 19 (31.6%) |

Every denominator is below one half, and so is the ceiling. That ceiling does not depend on how good the transform is: 9 of the 19 repairs touched no example fence at all, and 4 more changed only comments or string contents inside one.

## How the probe works (the module header is the authority)

- **Population.** Every `*.md` under `skills/objectstack-*` with `evals/` excluded: 49 files. A fence is in scope when the first token of its opener is `ts`, `typescript`, `tsx`, `json`, `json5`, `jsonc` or `yaml`/`yml`. `jsonc` is outside the dispatched list; it is admitted as JSON-with-comments and reported on its own column. Every other fence is counted as *other*.
- **Transform.** TS and JSON fences are parsed through `scripts/ts-parse.mjs` and never executed. Literals are evaluated statically. The supported shapes are `defineX({…})`, `X.create({…})` / `XSchema.parse({…})`, typed literals (`const a: T =`, `satisfies T`, `as T`), `key: value` fragments, bare literals and YAML documents. A fence that does not read as a whole is split at blank lines. Same-fence `const` bindings are followed, and `Field.kind(…)` runs on the spec's own pure helper. Anything else is **opaque**: issues at, under or above an opaque node are suppressed and counted, never guessed.
- **Mapping.** Mapping is tried in this order. (1) The code's own claim: the factory or constructor it calls, or the spec type it is annotated with. (2) An `os:check-yaml` marker's declaration. (3) Key ownership. Tier 1 is the one registry metadata type (or the stack) that declares every key, judged partially. Tier 2 is used only when tier 1 finds no owner: the one named schema the fragment is a complete instance of. A stack's map-format collections are normalised as `defineStack` normalises them. A component's `properties` is judged by its `ComponentPropsMap` row, the dispatch `check-yaml-examples` already performs. Schemas come from this tree's built `packages/spec/dist`, rebuilt first. The probe refuses a dist older than `src`.
- **Verdicts kept apart.**
  - *Structural red*: a Zod issue, reported per code.
  - *Counter-example*: code the text marks as wrong, either under a ❌ or "Incorrect" heading or with a leading ❌ comment. These are never a red and never a replay signature.
  - *Coverage miss*: a fence that is not read or not mapped, with its reason.

## Transform and mapping coverage

- **279 TypeScript fences.** The transform produced a value for **203 (72.8%)**. It missed 76: 67 `no-candidate` (runtime code such as hook bodies and engine calls, with no metadata literal) and 9 `syntax` (ellipsis placeholders and prose inside the fence).
- **Mapping.** Of the 203, 117 were mapped whole, 2 partly, and 86 not mapped: 46 `ambiguous-owner` and 40 `unmapped` (nested sub-schema fragments such as `where:` and node `config:`).
- **Whole.** 115 of the 279 TS fences (41.2%) were read **and** mapped whole; 117 of all 283 population fences (41.3%).
- **Mapped items by shape.** factory-call 45 · create-call 25 · property-list 39 · bare-literal 33 · typed-literal 6. By tier: 76 by the code's own claim, 60 by tier-1 ownership, 12 by tier-2 inference.
- **`os:check` blocks.** 33 skills fences carry the `os:check` marker. The probe judges 32 of them whole.

## Replay: the cards premise 1 counts

**The set.** The premise's own listing (`domain:skills`, `state=all`, `since=2026-09-23T00:00Z`, title regex as quoted) returns 116 issues across pages today, and 22 titles match. Two of them, #22120 and #22123, were created after #22059 was filed (2026-10-07T05:02Z), so **20 matched at filing, not 21**. The command as written reads page 1 only; today that page holds 21 matches, the two post-filing cards included and #18964 (page 2) excluded. All 12 ids the premise names are in the set.

**Method.** Each card's landing PR is the merged PR whose merge instant is the card's `closed` timeline event, located on `main` by its squash subject. Both sides are read from the local object store and judged by **this tree's** schemas, which is a stated bias in both directions. A fence is *touched* when its body is not found verbatim on the other side. A **HIT** is a structural signature on a touched BEFORE fence that no touched AFTER fence carries.

Notes:

1. Both HITs sit in blocks carrying the `os:check` marker. `check:skill-examples` type-checks those blocks, and it cannot see either error: a Zod refinement and an open `properties` record both type-check.
2. #20173's AFTER side is still red on today's schemas, for `page:header` `breadcrumb`, which was retired in spec 17 after that repair. The signature the repair removed is what makes it a HIT.
3. Counterfactual for the two `transform` misses. Judged by the `where` member of any of the four candidate schemas, both sides are accepted: that member accepts `{ status: { $foo: 1 } }` too. They would read `neither` with a perfect mapping.

## Control: the current catalog on this tree

| verdict | fences |
|:--|--:|
| green | 110 |
| red | 3 |
| counter-example | 4 |
| partly | 2 |
| coverage miss | 164 |

There are 14 issues suppressed as opaque or open. Counter-examples: 8 are refused, as their text says (`indexing.md` ×2, `lifecycle.md` ×5 rules, `relationships.md:382`). 2 are accepted by the schema; both are semantic ❌ (`relationships.md:351` lookup vs master_detail, `pagination.md:75` keyset field).

The three reds:

| site | verdict | reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md:77` (`os:check` block) | `custom` at `body` | **a teaching error on `main`**: `type: 'modal'` with a `body`. The built `defineAction` throws on it ("`body` only runs for `type: 'script'` …"). |
| `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md:176` | `custom` at `target` | **a teaching error on `main`**: `type: 'url'` with no `target`. `defineAction` throws "Action 'target' is required when type is 'url', …". |
| `skills/objectstack-upgrade/references/examples-upgrade.md:7` | `invalid_type` / `invalid_value` | a probe gap, not an error: the deliberate protocol-16 FROM shape the upgrade skill migrates |

The two `actions.md` sites are reported as findings for the seat to file. ⛔ This PR does not edit them. A control check confirms the existing gate misses the first one: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` is green on this head ("262 prose examples type-check across 3 surface(s)") with the `actions.md:77` block in it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Premise corrections (#22059's Dedupe paragraph and premise 1):**
  - Four existing gates already read example blocks, opt-in: `check:skill-examples` (`os:check`, TypeScript), `check:yaml-examples` (`os:check-yaml`), `check:doc-formula-expressions` and `check:doc-security-posture`.
  - The listing counts 20 cards at filing, not 21.
- **Probe gaps** a gate built on this probe would have to close:
  - an expect-red convention for the upgrade skill's FROM shapes;
  - the 86 ownership misses (nested fragments; ambiguous query fragments);
  - the `Plugin` type, held out by `TYPE_NOT_A_SPEC_SHAPE`.
- **Stated bias:** the replay is judged by today's schemas, not the schemas of each repair's own day.
- #13582, #13658, #14292 and #19715 remain as is. The 22 replayed cards remain as is.

## Verification (head `e6d00e1421`)

- `pnpm check:corpus-claim-drift`: exit 0. The self-test prints `OK` with the four `Probe …` batteries at 14/18/21/12 cases. The ratchet prints "OK, no new claim sites", over 252 files.
- `node scripts/check-corpus-claim-drift.mjs --probe-examples --json …`: exit 0, with the readings above. Apart from its head line, the output is byte-identical on every run from before the first commit to this head.
- One-off ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored with blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`:
  - opaque suppression disabled: self-test exit 1 (2 cases red);
  - the HIT rule disabled: exit 1 (1 case red);
  - the probe registration call disabled: exit 1 (all four probe batteries "DID NOT RUN").
- Gate families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on this head (30 commands): all exit 0, `check:pm-dispatch-gates` included.
- Roster families keyed under `scripts/`:
  - `check-published-list-mirrors` (both), `check:dts-closure`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:i18n-stale-fill` and `check-dts-references --self-test`: exit 0.
  - NOT MEASURED: `check:published-readme-exports`, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3, 45 packages unbuilt). `check:console-injection` skipped (no console dist).
- eslint, narrowed to the 2 touched files:
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reports 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - The population comes from `eslint.config.mjs` (`files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']`).
  - No `parserOptions.project` or typed rules are configured, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes`: exit 0. The control-byte self-scan of both files: none.
